title: The pack fingerprint takes file times from the directory listing, not one stat per file
goal: kbfacts.fingerprint() gives the same value as before (sha1 over path, mtime_ns and size of the same files in the same order) but reads the domain files' times and sizes from the directory listing (os.scandir) instead of one os.stat per file, which in a Hyper-V container costs about 0.7 ms per file (0.3 s of a 0.37 s warm pack, measured in python:3.14-windowsservercore-ltsc2025) and grew to seconds per pack under the CI job's load, where every pack outlasts FP_MEMO and recomputes it (test_spread_key_words_get_a_check_line 862 s, test_lookup_eval_passes 783 s, kb_ask and kb_hook past their 60 s); the memo counts from the end of the computation. A test holds the value equal to a per-file os.stat reference, and an mtime-only change of a root file changes it.
